newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis cut dollar component of forex borrowing.
newsitem.headline: Israelis cut dollar component of forex borrowing.

text.p: Dollar-borrowing by the Israeli private sector dropped sharply in the first four months of the year but overall foreign currency borrowing grew sharply, figures from the Bank of Israel released on Wednesday showed.

In January-April 1997, the dollar accounted for just 56 percent of foreign currency borrowing, down from 66 percent in 1996 and 78 percent in the two years prior to that, the central bank's supervisor of foreign currency said.

The bank said the pace of foreign currency borrowing picked up in the four months, as total new loans grew by $2.5 billion to a total of $28 billion at end of April 1997. Forex borrowing comprised one third of total credit, it said.
Between 1994 and 1996, forex currency credit, including actual forex loans and forex-linked loans, grew by nine billion dollars, the Bank of Israel said.
The central bank attributed the decline in dollar borrowing to interest rate differentials between the dollar and the yen and the Swiss franc.

During January-April 1997, borrowing in the yen and Swiss franc each accounted for 19 percent of total forex borrowing. The yen accounted for 18 percent of forex borrowing in 1996 and 13 percent in 1995, while the Swiss franc for nine percent and two percent, respectively.
